1 بَلَطَ , (IDrd, K,) [aor., accord. to a rule observed in the K,
بَلُطَ ,] inf. n. بَلْطٌ, (IDrd, TA,) He spread, or paved, (K, TA,) a house, (K,) and the ground, (TA,) with بَلَاط [or flag-stones], (K, TA,) or with baked bricks; (TA;) as also ↓ بلّط , (K,) inf. n. تَبْلِيطٌ; (TA;) and ↓ ابلط :
(K:) or, as also ↓ the second, he made [or constructed] a wall with بَلَاط: (IDrd, TA:) or ↓ the second, he made a house plain, or even. (TA.) ＝
-A2- He struck him, or it, with the بَلْط [q. v.]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
